sources.quote: 'The second Etruscan innovation is the intensive initial accent which also spread in Latin and the Italic languages, and which produced a larger number of syncopated words in Etruscan than in Latin. ... Around 500 the evidence of the inscriptions shows that a change took place in the way both Etruscan and Latin were pronounced, when the so-called initial stress accent came into Etruscan and Latin (as well as other languages of Italy). At this time all words were heavily stressed, or accented, on the first syllable. The rest of the word was proportionately less stressed, and vowels dropped out
sources.locator: ch. IV 'The pronunciation of Etruscan', pp. 80-81 (djvu txt lines ~5925-5975)

sources.citation: Skutsch, Franz (with G. Koerte). 1907. 'Etrusker' (II. Sprache), Paulys Realencyclopaedie der classischen Altertumswissenschaft VI,1, cols. 730-806. German Wikisource transcription (Korrekturstand: korrigiert).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.quote: 'Synkope von Binnensilben durch die Wirkung eines auf der ersten Silbe stehenden exspiratorischen Akzents: athrpa Atropos, atlenta Atalanta, achle Achilles, casntra Cassandra, clutmsta Klytaimestra, elchsntre ... Alexandros, hercle, menle Menelaos, menrva ...'; col. 788 notes a few Greek loans (mnele Menelaos, tlamunus Telamonios) that 'eine der griechischen entsprechende Akzentstelle vorauszusetzen scheint', and anaptyxis as a counter-tendency.
sources.locator: cols. 787-788 (treatment of Greek names, point gamma)

sources.quote: Sec. 1.4.1 gives the vowel and consonant systems (after Agostiniani 1992) with no statement of accent position. P. 239: 'Anche i fenomeni legati al cambio di accento sembrano procedere di pari passo: se il passaggio da melodico/libero a tonico sembra ancora in corso nel V sec. questo limite va pero spostato agli inizi del secolo, come ben dimostra il caso di avile/avele/avale ... Lo studio recente di Rigobianco (2017) richiama inoltre ulteriori aspetti morfotattici legati alla presenza di un accento secondario in eta arcaica.' Dates the onset of the stress accent (and syncope) to the early 5th
